subject: inconsistent results from DIF() sweep across items and manual item-by-item analysis

messages.author: 38b47219d8495cdc
messages.subject: inconsistent results from DIF() sweep across items and manual item-by-item analysis
parts:
Dear Colleagues,
We were conducting DIF analysis using the mirt package and ran into an issue where we got different results (1) when running DIF() to assess DIF sweeping through all items and (2) when analyzing item-by-item manually using multipleGroup(). 

The DIF() sweep returns results with large AIC and SABIC changes for all items, which seems unusual. So we did some spot checks and the manual check showed little changes in AIC and BIC for the two items we checked. I thought the results from the sweep and manual analyses should be the same. So I hope to be able to get some insights from you.

Thank you for your help in advance!
Best,
Shuting 

Here is our code for DIF testing. I also attached the files to reproduce the results.
########
library(tidyverse)
library(mirt)

useData <- readRDS("./comboDat.RDS")

# comment out line 20 and uncomment line 24 if you do not want to re-run the DIF-sweep that takes several hours!

set.seed(9644)
mirtCluster(4)
fit_sex_mod1 <- multipleGroup(data=useData[which(!is.na(useData$useChildSex)),str_detect(colnames(useData), "v3d")],
                              model=1,
                              group=as.factor(useData$useChildSex[which(!is.na(useData$useChildSex))]),
                              itemtype="graded",
                              invariance=c("free_means","free_vars","slopes","intercepts"),
                              method="MHRM",
                              SE=TRUE,
                              SE.type="MHRM",
                              technical=list(NCYCLES=5000, BURNIN=200, SEMCYCLES=150),
                              verbose=TRUE)
dropSex <- DIF(fit_sex_mod1, which.par=c("a1","d1","d2","d3"), scheme="drop", p.adjust='fdr') # note this runs for several hours

mirtCluster(remove = TRUE)

# dropSex <- readRDS("./dropSex.RDS") # in case you don't want to run that on its own!

dropSex # everything is highly significant

# but test just one item - spot-check examples

#spot check Item v3d001
testv3d001 <- multipleGroup(data=useData[which(!is.na(useData$useChildSex)),str_detect(colnames(useData), "v3d")],
                            model=1,
                            group=as.factor(useData$useChildSex[which(!is.na(useData$useChildSex))]),
                            itemtype="graded",
                            invariance=c("free_means","free_vars",
                                         colnames(useData)[which(str_detect(colnames(useData), "v3d") &
                                                                   colnames(useData) != "v3d001")]),
                            method="MHRM",
                            SE=TRUE,
                            SE.type="MHRM",
                            technical=list(NCYCLES=5000, BURNIN=200, SEMCYCLES=150),
                            verbose=TRUE)

anova(fit_sex_mod1, testv3d001) # delta-AIC is about 16, delta-BIC is about -7, but DIF sweep suggests diff is around -2400

# spot check v3d092

testv3d092 <- multipleGroup(data=useData[which(!is.na(useData$useChildSex)),str_detect(colnames(useData), "v3d")],
                            model=1,
                            group=as.factor(useData$useChildSex[which(!is.na(useData$useChildSex))]),
                            itemtype="graded",
                            invariance=c("free_means","free_vars",
                                         colnames(useData)[which(str_detect(colnames(useData), "v3d") &
                                                                   colnames(useData) != "v3d092")]),
                            method="MHRM",
                            SE=TRUE,
                            SE.type="MHRM",
                            technical=list(NCYCLES=5000, BURNIN=200, SEMCYCLES=150),
                            verbose=TRUE)

anova(fit_sex_mod1, testv3d092)

messages.subject: Re: inconsistent results from DIF() sweep across items and manual item-by-item analysis
parts:
I haven't finished running this yet on the latest version of the package, but was there any reason to be using the MHRM algorithm in this case? That's generally only useful when you are trying to fit a model with 4+ latent variables... After using the EM algorithm instead I don't see any significant results in the p_adjust column. Happy to run this again if it's related specifically to the MHRM, though that seems somewhat doubtful.

Phil
